pillar_reactions.evidence: He interrupted the pillar to establish how it would accommodate his knee, and answered his own question with his existing protocol: 'if I'm doing some squats, you know, with the kettlebells up here, and I have some knee pain, I will stop and I will put a band around my, just above my knees, which forces the knees in the right position, and that pain will go away, and I know how to do that, and I know I may have to add some of those leg exercises from my physical therapist years ago ... in addition to what you guys have.' He also volunteered the constraint before the rep could raise it — 'I don't want to do that, I'm old enough, my ego's gone' — on rushing to heavy bells.

The rep conceded the pillar before delivering it — 'From what you described, it sounds like it's already pretty good for you. So Trevor would mainly fine-tune it' — and the prospect agreed without questions, 'Yeah, that's important, yeah. Exactly.' He had already demonstrated more nutritional detail than the pillar contains, including glucose sequencing and a cholesterol reversal, so this pillar carried no persuasive weight in the sale.

The rep pitched it through an athlete-specific frame that landed — 'we had a lot of athletes also coming in when they're not in their training regime, they tend to fall off because there always was a coach who was saying, hey, you have to do this' — and the prospect completed the sentence himself: 'Yeah. And the belly is on.' No questions and no pushback, but it is the pillar that maps onto the gap he named, which was guidance and sequencing rather than motivation.

anchors.raw: Yeah. How much does it cost? 20 grand? If it was 20 grand.
anchors.note: The only anchor in the batch set above the offer. He guessed more than three times the six-month price before hearing it, which meant $6,000 landed as relief rather than resistance and no objection followed. This is what the ICP's income criterion is actually describing, and it is worth contrasting with the four prospects in this batch who anchored below.

anchors.raw: my therapist that he recommended me go to doctor PT, doctor. She also played soccer and was also a personal trainer. I called her triple PT ... I did it religiously because I wanted to get back to playing.
anchors.note: Nine months of paid one-to-one professional guidance that he valued and completed. He has a working reference class for what individual coaching is worth and, crucially, for complying with a programme he is paying for.

anchors.raw: I've been following Trevor's videos. I've been doing some of those workouts. I like the functional stuff. I love it. I love the kettlebells. I've got them sitting over here.
anchors.note: Fully equipped, already training with the modality, and pre-sold on the coach. Notably he uses the free content as evidence that the method suits him rather than as a reason not to pay — the exact opposite of how the same free content was used by the prospect on the other call this same day.

anchors.raw: So I went to a holistic cardiologist and he changed my diet and supplements. So I'm not on a pharmaceutical and mostly diet ... And his wife is a gastroenterologist.
anchors.note: An established pattern of paying specialists for health outcomes outside the insurance system. Nothing in his history suggests price sensitivity on health spending, and none appeared.

unmet_demand.want: His existing knee rehabilitation protocol integrated into the programme rather than run alongside it
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He assumed he would have to bolt it on himself — 'I may have to add that in, in addition to what you guys have' — and the rep answered generally, that Trevor prepares mobility work for weak points, without confirming that a PCL-deficient knee protocol from a named physiotherapist would be incorporated. It may well be served; it was not established either way.

unmet_demand.want: A clear explanation of the performance reward term in the agreement
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The prospect found it in the contract himself and the rep had not covered it — 'Yes, I didn't go over that' — and then described it as '$500 for an accolable purchase', which does not clearly state what the reward is, what qualifies, or when it pays.

unmet_demand.want: Certainty on what happens to a paid six-month programme if he is injured partway through
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered verbally with 'if you get an injury, we pause', which is not in the playbook and is not evidenced in the agreement he signed minutes later — an agreement he himself read as disclaiming responsibility for injuries.
